episodes.title: Reading the Script
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open the script for the next scene. You read through it slowly with a notebook beside you. You mark what locations, sets, and design requirements each page calls for.

episodes.title: Sketching the Set
episodes.text: You sit with the script notes, budget sheet, research photos, and location pictures. You compare what the story needs with what money and locations allow. You start shaping a set design that fits all four.

episodes.title: Drawing Floor Plans
episodes.text: You sit down to update the rough drafts and scale working drawings. You adjust the floor plans, scenery, and properties to be constructed. It is the same drawing work as yesterday, and the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Showing Plans for Approval
episodes.text: You bring your plans to review for approval.

choice.prompt: Your reviewer asks for a change before approving. What do you do?

options.label: Adjust the plan now to fit the purpose
options.outcome: You change the layout during the meeting. You leave with an approved direction to draw up cleanly.

options.label: Keep the plan and explain your purpose
options.outcome: You explain why the current plan serves the scene. You are asked to bring back a small revision tomorrow.

chat.text: Does this still work for the purpose of the scene?
Can you walk me through the layout once more?

episodes.title: Budget Cuts the Plan
episodes.text: You get word that the budget will not cover the build as drawn. You look at your approved plan against the new fabrication limit. You have to adapt the plan to fit what can actually be made.

choice.prompt: The set costs too much to build as drawn. How do you adapt it?

options.label: Simplify the build to meet budget
options.outcome: You redraw a smaller version using less construction. The plan now fits the budget and can be built.

options.label: Rework the plan around the location limits
options.outcome: You change the design to use more of the existing location. The build needs less fabrication work.

episodes.title: Final Rendering Details
episodes.text: You sit back down to finish the preliminary rendering of the revised idea. You add the construction notes, layout, and material specifications. You include a simple diagram for the lighting change.

trial.title: Order the rendering steps
items: Add diagrams for lighting
Draw the layout
List material specifications
Note the construction details
trial.explain: You lay out the idea first, then detail how it is built.

episodes.title: Morning Delivery Unload
episodes.text: You back up to the construction site with the truck loaded. You lift the prefabricated duct parts off the bed. You carry them inside for assembly and installation.

choice.prompt: The side door is blocked by lumber and the main entrance is clear but farther. What do you do?

options.label: Carry parts through the main entrance
options.outcome: You walk the longer path and stack the parts inside. It takes more trips but nothing gets damaged.

options.label: Wait for the side door to be cleared
options.outcome: You wait with the truck open until the crew moves the lumber. You start carrying parts a half hour late.

episodes.title: Cutting Duct Sections
episodes.text: You lay out flat sheet on the bench for the HVAC ducts. You cut and shape the pieces for a high efficiency system. You square the edges so they will fit tight later.

episodes.title: Checking Each Measurement
episodes.text: You pick up the calipers and measure a finished duct part. You check it against the scale and spec sheet. You set approved parts in one stack.

trial.title: Find the Bad Part
trial.scenario: You measure three duct sections with calipers. Two match the spec exactly. One section measures a quarter inch too narrow and will not join up.
options: The narrow section that will not join up
One of the sections that matches spec
The calipers themselves
trial.explain: You pull the narrow part before it causes a bad fit.

episodes.title: Riveting Seams Again
episodes.text: You sit at the bench fastening seams with rivets and clips. You set each rivet, check it, and slide the next section over. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Brake Press Stops
episodes.text: You press the pedal and the brake does not cycle. You open the guard and see the drive belt slipped off. Ducts are waiting on this machine.

choice.prompt: The belt is off but not broken. What do you do?

options.label: Reseat the belt and test it yourself
options.outcome: You fit the belt back on and run a test bend. The machine cycles and you get back to work.

options.label: Lock it out and get help first
options.outcome: You tag the machine off and bring the lead over. You both reseat the belt and check it together.

episodes.title: Sealing the Joints
episodes.text: You line up the duct joints with your coworker for final assembly. You hold the seam steady while he gets the rivet gun.

chat.text: Hold that joint tight for me?
I will drive rivets down this seam.
Then we can caulk it and call it done.

episodes.title: Starting Main Engines
episodes.text: You stand at the controls in the engine room. You start the main engines to get the ship moving. You regulate the power as the bridge orders a slow ahead.

choice.prompt: The bridge orders a lower speed. You watch the load drop. Do you adjust now?

options.label: Ease the throttle back now
options.outcome: You bring the speed down smooth. The bridge confirms the new speed.

options.label: Hold steady a moment longer
options.outcome: You wait and watch the gauges. You then ease back and steady the speed.

episodes.title: Watching the Gauges
episodes.text: You sit on watch and scan the same engine indicators. You log the readings and watch them hold steady. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Testing for a Fault
episodes.text: You stay with one pump that sounds off. You test its operation and watch the readings. You narrow down where the malfunction sits.

trial.title: Order the test steps
items: Trace what caused the fault
Note the normal readings
Spot where it malfunctions
Run a test on the equipment
trial.explain: You watch first, then test, then find the fault and its cause.

episodes.title: Checking Lifeboat Gear
episodes.text: You walk the deck with a crewmate to check lifesaving gear. You look at each station together.

chat.text: This raft strap looks loose to me.
Is the release clear on this side?
I will note it if you agree.

episodes.title: Fire Drill Below
episodes.text: The alarm sounds for the emergency drill. You move to your station in the machinery space. You work your part of the drill with the shipboard staff.

choice.prompt: The team leader calls your station during the drill. What do you do first?

options.label: Report your area status
options.outcome: You call in your readings and position. The team logs you in place.

options.label: Stay quiet and keep watching
options.outcome: You keep monitoring your equipment. You report in on the next call.

episodes.title: Logging the Day
episodes.text: You sit down and write up what you saw. You report one abnormal reading to shipboard staff. You note the pollution gear check for the record.

episodes.title: Morning System Checks
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and open the system dashboards. You scan CPU, memory, and error rates against the expected limits. Everything looks steady so far.

episodes.title: Same Log Review
episodes.text: You scroll through the same health checks you checked yesterday. You confirm the servers are still responding as specified. You close the tab and wait for the next interval.

episodes.title: Talking Through Limits
episodes.text: You join a call with a systems analyst and a programmer to pin down limits for a small change.

choice.prompt: They wait for you to decide how to get the missing interface detail.

options.label: Ask for the performance requirement now
options.outcome: You ask, they share the number, and you write it down for the design.

options.label: Say you will guess for now
options.outcome: You move on, but you still need to confirm the real limit later.

chat.text: We can add that check, but it will slow the response time.
Can you two confirm what the system can still handle?
If we keep the current interface, we stay inside the limit.

episodes.title: Checking What Fits
episodes.text: You read a short user request for a new report. You compare what is wanted with the time and cost you have. You note where the design will not fit.

trial.title: Spot the blocker
trial.scenario: A user asks for extra checks by Friday. The design needs two more weeks to build and test. The current time and cost cover only the simple version.
options: The design will not fit the time and cost limits
The dashboard colors look a little dull
The last install finished without issues
trial.explain: The time and cost limit is what makes the request not feasible as asked.

episodes.title: Install Hits Trouble
episodes.text: You are coordinating a software install when the monitors show the system is out of specification.

choice.prompt: The install is half done and errors are rising. What do you do?

options.label: Pause the install and hold the system steady
options.outcome: You pause the rollout and watch the monitors settle back toward normal.

options.label: Keep installing and watch closely
options.outcome: You continue the install while you keep checking the monitors for changes.

chat.text: Install is halfway through and errors are climbing.
Do we pause it or roll it forward?

episodes.title: Writing Test Notes
episodes.text: You sit back down and update the test steps for what you installed today. You write down what to check and what counts as passing. You save the notes for the team.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Sleep Technologist — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Numbers Check
episodes.text: You arrive and open your laptop at your desk. You pull up yesterday's customer data on age, needs, and buying habits. You sort through it to see who is still interested and why.

episodes.title: Talking Through Opinions
episodes.text: You sit down for a call with the marketing team to compare notes on customer opinions.

choice.prompt: The team waits for your read on the shift in opinions. What do you do?

options.label: Suggest a quick follow-up check with customers
options.outcome: You agree to run a short follow-up and bring the answers back tomorrow.

options.label: Stick with the current read for now
options.outcome: You keep the current view and note to watch the next answers closely.

chat.text: People seem to answer differently about price than last month.
Do you think our strategy still fits what they want?

episodes.title: Same Satisfaction Count
episodes.text: You open the same satisfaction tally you checked yesterday. You count the new scores and add them to the sheet. Same boxes, same numbers, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Broken Survey Link
episodes.text: You check the new survey and see answers have stopped coming in. The link for the opinion poll is not saving responses. You need to decide what to do before more time passes.

choice.prompt: Responses are stuck and the day is moving. What do you do first?

options.label: Pause the survey and fix the saving issue
options.outcome: You pause it, fix the save step, and test it before opening it again.

options.label: Use the answers you already have
options.outcome: You close this round early and work with the answers collected so far.

options.label: Switch to existing customer data instead
options.outcome: You set this survey aside and pull together existing data to cover the gap.

episodes.title: Shaping New Questions
episodes.text: You sit back down to work on the next questionnaire. You rewrite a few questions about preferences and needs. You keep the wording short so people can answer easily.

trial.title: Order the survey steps
items: Test the draft questions with a small group
Send the finished survey to customers
Write draft questions about needs and habits
Fix wording that confuses people
trial.explain: You write first, then test, fix, and send last.

episodes.title: Writing Up Findings
episodes.text: You turn your notes into a short report for the team. You add a simple chart to show the main findings. You write what the numbers mean in plain words.

episodes.title: First Family Visit
episodes.text: You sit down in the living room with a mother and her two kids. You ask about daily life and listen to what is hard right now.

chat.text: Money is tight and the kids are missing school a lot.
My youngest needs extra help and I do not know where to go.
Can you tell us what services we can get?

episodes.title: School Phone Call
episodes.text: You call the school and the child guidance clinic about a boy who faces problems at home and in class. You compare notes on his needs and support around his disability.

choice.prompt: The school and clinic disagree on what he needs first. Who do you bring in next?

options.label: Call family services and the school together
options.outcome: You set up a joint call. You agree on home visits and extra help at school.

options.label: Ask protective services to review safety
options.outcome: You send a referral for a safety check. You wait for their report before changing school support.

episodes.title: Updating Case Files
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and update case history records. You type visit notes into the same forms as yesterday. Same files again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Advising Foster Parents
episodes.text: You sit with new foster parents at their kitchen table. You explain temporary foster care and what daily care will look like. You answer their questions about rules and routines.

trial.title: Reassure new parents
trial.says: We are nervous about taking him even for a short stay. What should we expect?
options: You will figure it out on your own, just do your best.
Temporary care means a short stay with clear routines, and I will advise you and check in.
Keep him in his room most of the time so nothing goes wrong.
trial.explain: Advising foster parents means giving clear guidance and ongoing support.

episodes.title: Urgent Placement Call
episodes.text: You get a call that a child needs a safe place tonight. You check open foster homes and medical treatment options.

choice.prompt: You must place him now. Where does he go tonight?

options.label: Place him in the open foster home
options.outcome: You arrange transport to the foster home. You tell the parents he will arrive tonight.

options.label: Place him in the medical treatment center
options.outcome: You arrange admission to the treatment center. You note the placement and inform the family.

options.label: Wait until morning to decide
options.outcome: You keep him with staff overnight. You place him in the morning when more homes open.

chat.text: We have one foster home open for tonight.
The treatment center also has a bed if he needs medical care.

episodes.title: Court Liaison Check
episodes.text: You stop by family court to share updates with a court contact. You connect the court, the school, and family services on one child's case. You confirm the next steps for support.

episodes.title: Morning Check In
episodes.text: You sit down and join the morning call. The others join from their kitchens and desks.

chat.text: Morning. The interface still has that limit we talked about.
Can you walk through performance needs with me?
I need to know what this design can and can't do.

episodes.title: Reading User Needs
episodes.text: You open the list of user needs and software requirements. You read line by line and compare them to time and cost. You mark what fits and what does not.

choice.prompt: One request will not fit in the time you have. What do you do?

options.label: Flag it as not feasible now
options.outcome: You mark it out of scope for this round. The list gets shorter and clearer.

options.label: Keep it in and note the risk
options.outcome: You leave it in with a note about time and cost. The team sees the risk up front.

episodes.title: Watching The Monitors
episodes.text: You check the equipment status screen. Everything says normal. You keep watching and log the same normal readings as yesterday.

episodes.title: Running The Tests
episodes.text: You sit with the software system testing procedures. You run the checks and write down what passes. You fix a small piece of programming where it fails.

trial.title: Order the test
items: Note what passes and what fails
Fix the programming where it fails
Write down what the test should check
Run the test on the system
trial.explain: You plan the check first, then you run it and record and fix.

episodes.title: Installation Stalls
episodes.text: You are coordinating the installation of the software system. Halfway through, the system does not operate as specified. Everyone waits for your call.

choice.prompt: The install is stuck and the system is not right. What do you do first?

options.label: Pause the install and check the system
options.outcome: You stop the install. You check the system against the specifications to find the fault.

options.label: Roll back and try again later
options.outcome: You undo this install step. The system goes back to how it was before.

episodes.title: Writing It Down
episodes.text: You open the documentation file. You add what you tested and installed today. You save it and close the laptop.

episodes.title: Walking the Roof
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and climb the ladder with a tape measure. You check the roof face for south orientation and open sun. You look at the shingles and rafters for solid structure.

choice.prompt: A big tree shades the west end of the best-facing roof. What do you do?

options.label: Mark the shaded end as unusable
options.outcome: You mark a smaller array on the sunny part. The system will be smaller but get full sun.

options.label: Shift the layout east
options.outcome: You sketch the rows farther east to clear the shade. You note the new measurements for the crew.

episodes.title: Building the Racks
episodes.text: You lay out rails and bolts on the roof by the drawings. You set the support feet in a straight line. You tighten each bracket and check it sits square.

episodes.title: More Bolts Again
episodes.text: You sit on the roof and bolt another rail together. You pass panels up, set them, tighten them, repeat. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Setting the Panels
episodes.text: You follow the schematic taped to your clipboard. You lift each panel onto the rails with a partner. You wire it in and torque the clamps to spec.

episodes.title: Loose Wire Found
episodes.text: You smell hot plastic near the inverter box.

choice.prompt: You see a bare wire end near the grounded box. What do you do first?

options.label: Stop and lock off power
options.outcome: You open the disconnect and tag it off. You wait until the meter reads zero before you go closer.

options.label: Tape it and keep working
options.outcome: You leave it live and reach in with tape. You risk a shock and the wire stays unsafe.

options.label: Call it out and rope off
options.outcome: You step back and tell the crew to stay clear. Your lead comes over to check the hazard with you.

chat.text: What do you see at the disconnect?
Check for heat, bare copper, and bad grounding before you touch anything.

episodes.title: Final Wiring Check
episodes.text: You walk the string with your meter. You test each termination for a tight fit. You confirm polarity and grounding before you pack up.

trial.title: Find the fault
trial.scenario: You test the last string. The meter reads negative voltage. The wires look tight and the ground looks solid.
options: Positive and negative leads are reversed
The panel glass is dusty
The rail bolts are too tight
trial.explain: Negative voltage means the polarity is swapped.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Sommelier — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Setting the Room
episodes.text: You arrive and select the settings on the ultrasound machine for the morning list. You help your first patient onto the table and adjust their position to get the best angle. You check the probe and the screen before you start.

episodes.title: Watching the Image
episodes.text: You move the probe slowly and watch the screen for a clear picture. You make small adjustments to the equipment when the image fades. You hold the view steady when it looks satisfactory for diagnosis.

trial.title: Spot the Problem
trial.scenario: You watch the screen during the scan. The image looks pale and unclear for diagnosis. You have not touched the equipment controls yet.
options: Adjust the equipment to make the image satisfactory
Send the unclear image on as it is
Ask the patient to fix the equipment
trial.explain: You keep watching the screen and adjust the equipment until the image is satisfactory.

episodes.title: Same Scans Again
episodes.text: You run the same ultrasound scans again. You produce and record the same kind of images. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking She Is Okay
episodes.text: You pause mid-exam to check on your patient.

choice.prompt: She looks uncomfortable on the table. What do you do now?

options.label: Pause and comfort her
options.outcome: You stop the probe, cover her, and explain what is left. She settles and you finish the exam safely.

options.label: Keep scanning without stopping
options.outcome: You keep moving the probe and finish faster. She stays tense through the rest of the exam.

chat.text: I feel a bit cold and nervous.
Is it supposed to take this long?

episodes.title: Image Will Not Clear
episodes.text: You watch the screen and the image stays grainy and incomplete. You try small adjustments but it is still not satisfactory for diagnosis. The patient waits quietly while you work on it.

choice.prompt: The image is still not good enough. What do you do?

options.label: Keep adjusting the equipment
options.outcome: You change the settings and reposition the probe. The image clears enough to record for the physician.

options.label: Record the poor image anyway
options.outcome: You save the grainy images and move on. The physician may ask for the scan to be repeated.

episodes.title: Sending the Findings
episodes.text: You save the sonogram images from the day. You write a short summary of the technical findings. You send both to the physician for diagnosis.

episodes.title: Morning Setup Check
episodes.text: You arrive early and walk the room. You set up the recording equipment for the day session. You test each line and adjust the knobs until it holds.

episodes.title: Talking Through Sound
episodes.text: You sit down with the producer before anyone plays.

chat.text: I want the vocal close and warm for this one.
Keep the guitar back, not too bright.
Can you get us that balance today?

episodes.title: First Recording Take
episodes.text: You sit behind the glass as the band starts. You record the music on the recording equipment. You watch the take roll and keep it clean.

choice.prompt: The guitar is louder than the agreed sound. Do you stop or keep recording?

options.label: Stop and talk it through
options.outcome: You stop the take. You reset the level and start again with the agreed sound.

options.label: Keep recording as is
options.outcome: You let the take finish. You have a loud guitar printed on the recording to deal with later.

options.label: Lower it quietly mid-take
options.outcome: You ease the fader down. The take continues with a smoother balance.

episodes.title: Watching The Levels
episodes.text: You sit at the control console after lunch. You regulate the volume level and sound quality. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Separating The Mix
episodes.text: You sit down for the postproduction pass. You pull up the tracks and separate the instruments, vocals, and other sounds. You start to combine them into a steady mix.

trial.title: Order the mix pass
items: Combine the sounds during the mix
Separate the vocals
Separate the other sounds
Separate the instruments
trial.explain: You separate each part first, then you combine them.

episodes.title: Losing Good Sound
episodes.text: You are in a recording session when the sound quality turns thin. You check the control console and the recording equipment fast.

choice.prompt: The take is still running and the sound is off. What do you do first?

options.label: Pause and readjust the equipment
options.outcome: You stop for a minute. You test and adjust the setup, then you roll again with clean sound.

options.label: Ride the console to fix it live
options.outcome: You stay with the take. You regulate volume and quality on the console until it steadies.

episodes.title: Opening the Rooms
episodes.text: You arrive before the first guest and open the schedule board. You look at rooms and times and move blocks to fill gaps. You keep the day tight so nothing sits empty long.

episodes.title: Morning Phone Messages
episodes.text: You sit down with overnight messages and call back two guests with questions. One wants to change a time and you check what is open.

choice.prompt: Both guests want the same late slot and only one fits. Who do you offer it to first?

options.label: Offer it to the first caller
options.outcome: You book the first caller in and offer the second caller the next open slot. The book stays fair and clear.

options.label: Hold it and call back later
options.outcome: You tell both guests you will confirm shortly. You check the facility schedule again before you decide.

episodes.title: Booking the Book
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and fill guest appointments one after another. You type names and times into the same slots you filled yesterday. You do the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Unhappy Guest Speaks
episodes.text: A guest comes to the desk unhappy about a mix-up with their appointment.

choice.prompt: The guest is upset and waiting for an answer. What do you do now?

options.label: Listen and offer a fix today
options.outcome: You hear the complaint out and find the nearest workable time or adjustment. The guest leaves with a clear plan.

options.label: Check the record first
options.outcome: You pull up the appointment and database to see what was booked. You come back with facts before you decide.

chat.text: I was told ten, but now you say eleven?
I took time off for this.

episodes.title: Fixing Client Records
episodes.text: You open the client database in the quiet afternoon. You review names, phones, and past visits for errors. You save each fix before you move on.

trial.title: Spot the conflict
trial.scenario: You check tomorrow's list against the client database. Two records look fine. One guest shows booked for two appointments at the same time.
options: The guest booked twice at once
A record with a full phone number
A record with a correct name
trial.explain: The double booking blocks the schedule and needs fixing first.

episodes.title: Counting Today's Cash
episodes.text: You close the door and count today's cash and receipts. You record the cash flow and prepare the bank deposit. You file the slip with today's statement.

episodes.title: Setting Out Morning Tables
episodes.text: You arrive early and unlock the classroom. You pull out bins of learning materials and set them on the low tables. You check that everything is within reach for small hands to explore and use.

trial.title: Set up the room
items: Students explore and handle the materials at the tables
You pull bins of learning materials from the shelf
You lay out the resources on the tables for the morning activity
You check that pieces are complete and within reach
trial.explain: You gather first, check, lay out, then children use them.

episodes.title: Sounding Out Words
episodes.text: You sit down with a small group for reading. You say each sound slowly and have them repeat it back with you. You pass out letter cards so they can see, touch, and say the sounds together.

episodes.title: Practicing Taking Turns
episodes.text: You sit with two students for turn-taking practice. You praise calm asking and guide them to try again when voices rise. You give each child a short turn and name what they did right.

choice.prompt: One student grabs the toy and does not let go. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and practice asking again
options.outcome: You model the words and they try again. The turn moves on slowly.

options.label: Give praise for the small try
options.outcome: You name the calm part and give another short turn. They stay with the practice.

episodes.title: Afternoon Repetition Practice
episodes.text: You sit at the same table with the same word cards. You go through them again, the same way as yesterday. Same cards tomorrow.

episodes.title: When Voices Rise
episodes.text: You are in the corner area when a disagreement turns loud.

choice.prompt: A student is upset and shouting after pushing materials off the table. What do you do first?

options.label: Move him aside and calm first
options.outcome: You sit nearby and wait until his breathing slows. Then you talk about what to do next.

options.label: Pick up the materials together
options.outcome: You kneel down and hand him one block at a time. You clean up side by side before you talk.

options.label: Practice the right words now
options.outcome: You model a calm ask and have him repeat it. You praise the calm try and go back to play.

chat.text: He pushed the blocks off the table.
Can you step in? I have the rest of the group.

episodes.title: Adjusting Tomorrows Lessons
episodes.text: You sit at your desk after the students leave. You look at tomorrow's elementary lesson and cross out parts to change. You write in simpler steps and extra repetition to meet their needs.

episodes.title: Morning Group Lesson
episodes.text: You arrive to a small room of chairs in a circle. You greet the group and start with a short lecture on pacing. You show them how a pause sounds, then you let them try it.

trial.title: Order the group lesson
items: You let the group try the skill
You explain the point briefly
You talk through what worked
You show how it sounds
trial.explain: You explain first, then show it, then they try it.

episodes.title: Watching Each Speaker
episodes.text: You sit to the side with your notebook while each person speaks.

chat.text: I always rush the ending. Is that bad?
You note it down and keep watching.
I really want to get better at the middle part too.

episodes.title: Changing the Plan
episodes.text: You sit with one student who is stuck on the group material. You see the lecture format is not landing for her. You pause and rework how you will explain it.

choice.prompt: She looks lost and bored. How do you change the lesson for her?

options.label: Switch to a short discussion about her interests
options.outcome: She talks about her weekend job and you tie pacing to that story.

options.label: Repeat the same lecture more slowly
options.outcome: She nods politely but still struggles with the next try.

episodes.title: Same Opening Drill
episodes.text: You run the same opening line drill you ran yesterday. Everyone stands, says the first line, and sits down. You say the same reminders again. It will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Nerves Before Going On
episodes.text: One student freezes in practice and wants to skip the hard speech. You stay beside him while the room waits. You remind him this is the challenging part to push through.

choice.prompt: He says he wants to quit for today. What do you do?

options.label: Encourage him to try one small part again
options.outcome: He gets through the opening and sits down breathing fast but calmer.

options.label: Let him sit out and watch the rest
options.outcome: He watches quietly and you check in with him after class.

options.label: Offer an easier extra practice to explore later
options.outcome: He takes the practice sheet and agrees to try it before next time.

episodes.title: Updating Student Records
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk with the attendance and notes. You write down what each student did today. You check that every record is complete before you leave.

episodes.title: Morning Speech Testing
episodes.text: You arrive and set out the picture cards. You sit down across from your first client. You give the oral test and note the sounds they miss.

trial.title: Spot the Priority
trial.scenario: You test a young child for delayed language. She uses very few words and coughs when she drinks water. Her test sheet shows limited sounds.
options: Swallowing safety needs attention first
Voice pitch needs attention first
Stuttering needs attention first
trial.explain: Trouble swallowing can be unsafe, so you check that before anything else.

episodes.title: Talking Through the Plan
episodes.text: You sit with a parent to go over the stuttering plan. You explain what the doctor suggested for school days.

choice.prompt: He stutters most in class. What do you start with?

options.label: Start with slow, short practice phrases
options.outcome: You practice short phrases with him. You write that into his treatment plan.

options.label: Hold the school practice for now
options.outcome: You keep treatment to the quiet room only. You note to revisit school practice next week.

chat.text: Will this plan help his stuttering at school?
How often will he practice at home?
What do we do if he gets stuck?

episodes.title: Same Notes Again
episodes.text: You check the progress charts. You mark the same boxes as yesterday. You stack them for tomorrow.

episodes.title: Writing Progress Reports
episodes.text: You sit down to write up the morning evaluations. You log treatment and progress notes for billing. You close out one discharge file.

episodes.title: Swallow Check Turns Urgent
episodes.text: You review a barium swallow result before your next visit. You see a swallowing problem that looks unsafe. Your patient coughs on every sip of water.

choice.prompt: The swallow looks unsafe right now. What do you do?

options.label: Stop the sip practice and change the plan
options.outcome: You stop the drinking task. You switch to a safer swallowing plan and note the change.

options.label: Keep the sip practice but watch closely
options.outcome: You stay with him and keep sips very small. You write down each cough for the doctor.

options.label: Pause and call the doctor first
options.outcome: You pause the session and share the result. You wait for guidance before you go on.

episodes.title: Adjusting the Voice Work
episodes.text: You listen to your teen client read aloud. Her voice still sounds harsh and low. You change the practice to easier pitch work.

episodes.title: Setting Up Morning Practice
episodes.text: You arrive early and lay out cones for today's practice. You check your plan for drills and time for each part. You tape the list to your clipboard and wait for the group.

episodes.title: Talking Through Nerves
episodes.text: You pull one athlete aside before drills. She looks tired and unsure about Saturday.

chat.text: Coach, I didn't sleep much last night.
I'm worried I'll mess up in the game.
What should I eat before we play?

episodes.title: Same Midday Drills
episodes.text: You run the same passing and footwork loop you ran yesterday. You count reps and fix the same spots. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Fixing Foot Placement
episodes.text: You watch the group practice starts and stops. You show one player how to shift weight through the feet. You have her try it again slow, then at speed.

trial.title: Spot what needs fixing
trial.scenario: You watch three players run the same move. One follows the rules but is slow. One moves fast but places the feet wrong and keeps slipping.
options: Tell the slow player to rest
Fix the foot placement that causes slipping
Change the rules for the drill
trial.explain: Wrong foot placement breaks the move, so you fix that first.

episodes.title: A Starter Falls Apart
episodes.text: You watch your planned starter miss passes and lose focus in the scrimmage. The game is tomorrow and you need a steady lineup. You have to choose who starts.

choice.prompt: Your planned starter is off today. Who do you start tomorrow?

options.label: Stick with the planned starter
options.outcome: She starts tomorrow. She may settle or she may struggle again.

options.label: Start the backup who practiced well
options.outcome: The backup starts tomorrow. The starter sits and waits for her turn.

episodes.title: Changing How You Coach
episodes.text: You sit with two players after practice to plan for tomorrow. One needs clear steps, the other shuts down with too much talk. You decide how to coach each one.

choice.prompt: How do you coach these two different players tomorrow?

options.label: Give both the same short instructions
options.outcome: You keep it simple for both. One gets what she needs and the other stays quiet.

options.label: Give one step-by-step cues and the other space
options.outcome: You talk more with the first player and less with the second. You watch how each responds.

episodes.title: Morning Sink Scrub
episodes.text: You arrive and pull on gloves at the sink. You scrub used instruments under the water. You rinse them and set them out for sterilization.

episodes.title: Same Instruments Again
episodes.text: You sit back at the sink with another batch of instruments. You scrub, rinse, and lay them out. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Building the Tray
episodes.text: You stand at the table building a routine surgical tray. You count and place each clean instrument in its spot. A slip asks for extra supplies for a special request.

choice.prompt: You are one instrument short for the special request. What do you do now?

options.label: Hold the tray and wait for the next cleaned batch
options.outcome: You set the tray aside and finish it when clean instruments come out. The tray goes out complete but late.

options.label: Send the tray out one piece short
options.outcome: You send the tray with a note about the missing piece. Staff have to call down for it later.

episodes.title: Checking for Wear
episodes.text: You walk the equipment and look over each sterilizer. You check for leaks around doors and pipes. You feel for worn or loose parts.

trial.title: Spot the Problem
trial.scenario: You examine a sterilizer before a load. One joint is dry and tight. Another fitting is loose and dripping water.
options: The loose fitting dripping water
The dry and tight joint
The clean outer wall
trial.explain: A loose part with a leak needs attention before the machine runs.

episodes.title: Hissing Autoclave Door
episodes.text: You load the steam autoclave and shut the door. You hear hissing and see steam leaking at the seal.

choice.prompt: The loaded autoclave is leaking steam at the door. What do you do?

options.label: Stop the cycle and check the seal
options.outcome: You abort the load and leave the door shut to cool. You check the seal for wear once it is safe.

options.label: Let the cycle finish leaking
options.outcome: You let it run and the load does not sterilize properly. You have to re-run the whole load.

options.label: Unload it hot and reseat the seal
options.outcome: You open the hot door and get blasted with steam. You have to reload and start over.

chat.text: Stop the load?
Do not run it leaking. Check the seal.

episodes.title: Logging the Loads
episodes.text: You sit down with the log after the run. You write down the sterilizer test result. You record what was in the load and the maintenance you did.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Streamer / Content Creator — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Reading Today's Blueprints
episodes.text: You arrive and open the blueprints for the floor pour. You count rods and check sizes, shapes, and where each one goes.

choice.prompt: One mark on the sketch is hard to read. What do you do?

options.label: Ask for clarification before counting
options.outcome: You wait a few minutes and get the right count. You start with the correct number of rods.

options.label: Guess and keep counting
options.outcome: You cut and stage the wrong number. You have to recount after the foreman checks.

episodes.title: Cutting Rods Down
episodes.text: You carry rods to the cutting area. You cut them to the lengths on the sheet with the bar cutter. You stack the cut pieces by size.

episodes.title: Tying The Grid
episodes.text: You sit by the forms and tie rods together with wire and pliers. You space each one, tie it, and move to the next. It is the same tie you did yesterday.

episodes.title: Blocking Up Rebar
episodes.text: You walk the deck placing blocks under the rebar. You lift each bar just enough to slide the block in. You set the bars back down on the blocks.

trial.title: Check The Supports
trial.scenario: You check a section of floor rebar before the pour. Most bars sit up on blocks off the deck. One bar rests flat on the deck with no block under it.
options: The bar sitting flat on the deck
A bar tied tight with wire
A bar cut to the right length
trial.explain: Rebar must sit up on blocks so concrete gets under it.

episodes.title: Setting Steel In Forms
episodes.text: You work with another ironworker to set mesh in the forms.

chat.text: Hold your side up while I get the fastener on.
Got it. Can you check if it is flat now?

episodes.title: Loose Bars Shifting
episodes.text: You see a few tied rods have shifted and sit crooked in the form. The pour is coming and they need to hold position.

choice.prompt: The ties are loose and bars have moved. What do you do first?

options.label: Re-space the rods and re-tie them tight
options.outcome: You pull the bars back to the blueprint spacing and fasten them. They stay put for the pour.

options.label: Leave them and keep placing blocks
options.outcome: The bars stay out of place in the form. Someone has to come back and fix them.

episodes.title: Opening Patient Files
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down at your desk. You open yesterday's notes and update histories and progress reports. You check that services provided are written down correctly.

episodes.title: New Faces Orientation
episodes.text: You stand at the front of a small room with new clients. You walk through what the chemical dependency program covers. You answer basic questions about what happens next.

episodes.title: Midmorning Sample Round
episodes.text: You collect urine samples one after another. You label each cup and set it aside. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Sitting With One Client
episodes.text: You sit across from your client for an individual session. He looks down and stops talking.

choice.prompt: He goes quiet. What do you do next in the session?

options.label: Give him space, then ask what feels hardest today
options.outcome: He pauses, then starts talking about his mornings at home.

options.label: Suggest ending early and trying again next time
options.outcome: He nods and leaves, and you note the short session in his record.

chat.text: I don't know if I can keep adjusting to all this.
Everything outside feels too much right now.

episodes.title: Afternoon Group Circle
episodes.text: You pull your chair into the group circle. You listen as each person shares about making changes. You help keep the talk steady and respectful.

trial.title: Answer with care
trial.says: I messed up this week and I'm scared to say it here.
options: Thank you for telling us. Do you want to share what happened?
You should have tried harder after last week's talk.
Let's skip you and come back if there is time.
trial.explain: The first reply keeps the group safe and supports honest sharing.

episodes.title: Checking On Discharged Client
episodes.text: You call a discharged patient to check how treatment is holding. She does not pick up the first time. You try again and she answers sounding shaky.

choice.prompt: She says she missed her aftercare and feels like slipping. What do you do?

options.label: Stay on the line and talk through a next step
options.outcome: She stays talking and agrees to come in tomorrow morning.

options.label: Ask if she wants a callback later this week
options.outcome: She says okay and hangs up, and you log the call for follow-up.

options.label: Encourage her to contact her support person now
options.outcome: She finds the number and says she will call them right after.

episodes.title: Scrubbing In Early
episodes.text: You arrive and change into surgical clothing. You scrub your arms and hands at the sink. You help the team pull on gloves, masks, and gowns.

episodes.title: Getting Patient Settled
episodes.text: You walk into the operating room with the nurse. You help move the patient onto the operating table. You position them and cover them with sterile drapes.

choice.prompt: The patient is on the table and the drapes are in your hands. What do you adjust first?

options.label: Check their position on the table, then place the drapes
options.outcome: You check their arms and legs are supported, then lay the drapes to cover exposed skin.

options.label: Place the drapes first, then shift their position
options.outcome: You lay the drapes down, then have to lift them again to fix a shoulder that is hanging off the edge.

episodes.title: Holding The Sterile Field
episodes.text: You sit by the instrument table as surgery starts. You watch the edges of the drapes and trays. You keep everything sterile and untouched by anything unclean.

episodes.title: Passing Instruments Again
episodes.text: You stand and hand instruments to the surgeon when asked. It is the same passes as yesterday. It will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Drape Edge Slips
episodes.text: You see the drape slip near the edge of the sterile field. The surgeon keeps working.

choice.prompt: The sterile drape has slipped. What do you do right now?

options.label: Speak up and fix the sterile field right away
options.outcome: You call it out and replace the drape. The team pauses for a minute, then goes on with clean cover.

options.label: Wait and watch to see if it gets worse
options.outcome: You keep watching. The exposed edge stays open and the nurse has to stop the case to redo it.

chat.text: Did that edge just move?
That corner looks off the sterile area now.

episodes.title: Counting Everything Twice
episodes.text: You stay at the table after the operation ends. You count sponges, needles, and instruments with the nurse. You check the after count against the before count.

trial.title: Put the count in order
items: Count sponges, needles, and instruments after the operation
Report the final counts to the nurse
Lay out sponges, needles, and instruments for the starting count
Count sponges, needles, and instruments before the operation
trial.explain: You always count the same set before and after so nothing is left behind.

episodes.title: Setting Up Practice
episodes.text: You arrive early on the pool deck. You spread your notes on the bench and map the practice in blocks. You set the lane order and times before anyone changes.

trial.title: Order the practice session
items: You run the main practice set
You write the plan for the session
You close with an easy cool-down
You start the group warm-up
trial.explain: You plan first, then warm up, work, and cool down.

episodes.title: Encouraging Tired Swimmers
episodes.text: You stand at the lane end as the group finishes a hard set. You call out direction for the next effort and urge them to hold form. You remind one swimmer out loud that her turns are getting cleaner.

choice.prompt: One swimmer hangs on the lane rope and wants to quit the set early. What do you do?

options.label: Stay with her for one more lap
options.outcome: You walk the deck beside her lane and talk her through one easy lap. She finishes the lap and climbs out to rest.

options.label: Let her sit out and watch
options.outcome: You nod and let her sit on the bench while the rest swim. She watches the set and rejoins for the cool-down.

episodes.title: Same Kick Drill
episodes.text: You run the same kick drill you ran yesterday. You count the laps and correct the same foot position. You will run it again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Adjusting Each Stroke
episodes.text: You work one on one with two swimmers after lunch. You watch how each moves hands and feet through the water. You change your cues so one works on reach and the other works on kick.

episodes.title: Last Minute Team Change
episodes.text: You check the list for Saturday's relay and learn one swimmer is sick. You look at who is ready and who needs more time. You must choose the four to swim.

choice.prompt: Your fastest swimmer is out sick for the relay. Who swims in her place?

options.label: Pick the next fastest swimmer
options.outcome: You slot in the next fastest swimmer and tell the group the new order. The team practices two exchanges with the new lineup.

options.label: Pick the steadier starter
options.outcome: You pick the swimmer with cleaner starts and explain the change. The group runs the start twice with her in the lead leg.

options.label: Split the legs differently
options.outcome: You move everyone up one leg and put a newer swimmer on the last leg. You walk them through the new plan on deck.

episodes.title: Food And Rest Talk
episodes.text: You gather the group after practice for a short talk. You explain what to eat and drink before Saturday's meet. You remind them about sleep and warming up on time.

episodes.title: Morning Call With Engineering
episodes.text: You join the video call and open your notes. The production engineer starts to explain the new production method.

choice.prompt: The engineer describes the steps fast and you miss one detail. What do you do?

options.label: Ask him to repeat the missed step
options.outcome: He repeats the step slowly and you write it down correctly. The call runs a few minutes longer.

options.label: Keep listening and check journals later
options.outcome: You finish on time and look up the detail in a journal article after the call. You add a note to confirm it tomorrow.

chat.text: Morning. The assembly order changed last week, so the old steps are out of date.
Want me to walk through the new sequence now while you take notes?

episodes.title: Organizing Today's Draft
episodes.text: You sit down with your interview notes and the outline. You arrange everything into order and start the writing assignment. You keep each sentence short and check your terms as you go.

trial.title: Put the draft together
items: Check style and terminology for consistency
Gather interview notes and source material
Write a concise draft from the arranged material
Arrange the material in clear order
trial.explain: You gather first, then order, write, and check style last.

episodes.title: Choosing The Diagram
episodes.text: You open the folder of drawings and charts for this section. You compare a sketch and a diagram side by side. You pick the diagram that shows the step most clearly.

episodes.title: Editing A Coworker Draft
episodes.text: You open a short draft written by another writer on the team. You read through and mark places where wording and terms do not match. You edit the lines so the style is standard and clear.

episodes.title: Filing Revisions Again
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and save today's files. You rename each version and put it in the same folders as yesterday. You close the folders when you are done.

episodes.title: Last Change Before Release
episodes.text: You get a message that one section must be fixed before the end of the day. The wording is unclear and does not follow the set standard. You open the file and see the clock moving.

choice.prompt: You have little time to fix the section. How do you handle it?

options.label: Fix the wording now to meet the standard
options.outcome: You rewrite the unclear lines and save the corrected version. The file goes out on time with your initials on the change.

options.label: Flag the lines and send it back
options.outcome: You mark the unclear lines and return the file with a short note. The release waits until someone else clears the wording.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Telecommunications Equipment Installer — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

episodes.title: Checking the bare floor
episodes.text: You arrive and kneel on the bare floor. You press your hand flat to feel if it is firm. You look close to see if it is dry.

choice.prompt: One corner feels soft and still damp. What do you do?

options.label: Start covering anyway
options.outcome: You lay over the damp spot. It stays soft under the covering.

options.label: Flag it and wait
options.outcome: You leave that corner alone. It has time to dry before you cover it.

episodes.title: Same sweeping again
episodes.text: You sweep the base surface clean. You scrape and sand the rough spots. You chip at a bump. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Building smooth foundation
episodes.text: You lay plywood over the floor to make it smooth. You staple it down flat. You brush waterproof compound on and fill the cracks with plaster.

trial.title: Spot what needs work
trial.scenario: You brushed compound on the surface. You look over the floor. One crack is still open and the pores are not sealed.
options: Sweep the clean corner again
Fill the open crack with plaster
Cut tile for the doorway
trial.explain: The open crack still needs filling to seal the surface.

episodes.title: Cutting around pipes
episodes.text: You measure tile around the pipes by the wall.

chat.text: That pipe is tight to the wall. Got enough room?
Cut it close so it fits around the obstruction.
Hold it up and I will mark the curve.

episodes.title: Joint will not close
episodes.text: You trim the excess edge and push two sections together. A gap stays open and will not form a tight joint. You hold the loose edge down with your hand.

choice.prompt: The sections will not make a tight joint. What do you do now?

options.label: Trim a sliver more and rejoin
options.outcome: You trim again and push the sections tight. The joint closes.

options.label: Tack the edge down gapped
options.outcome: You tack the edge with the gap still showing. It stays open.

options.label: Stop and check the cut
options.outcome: You stop and look at the edge. You see where it is catching.

episodes.title: Tacking the edges
episodes.text: You trim the last excess covering. You tack the edges down flat. You join the sections into a tight joint.

episodes.title: Checking Your Truck
episodes.text: You arrive and walk around your truck in the cold. You check the brakes, lights, and tires. You open the box and check the safety and emergency gear.

trial.title: Secure the Load
items: Tighten the binders to take up slack
Set the blocks around the cargo
Pull the cover over the load
Run the chain over the cargo
trial.explain: You block it first, then chain it, tighten it, and cover it last.

episodes.title: Chaining Down Cargo
episodes.text: You climb up and set blocks tight against the cargo. You throw chain over it and work the binders tight. You pull a cover on and tie it down with rope.

episodes.title: Same Check Again
episodes.text: You walk the same loop around the load. You tug the same chains and look at the same blocks. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Dangerous Load Talk
episodes.text: You stop before you roll with a dangerous load and call your boss.

choice.prompt: The papers do not clearly match the dangerous load. Do you roll or wait?

options.label: Wait and recheck safety steps
options.outcome: You stay parked and go back through the safety steps and papers line by line.

options.label: Roll and sort it later
options.outcome: You drive off with a mismatch and risk a stop and a spill you cannot handle.

chat.text: What placards and papers do you have for that load?
Walk me through your safety steps before you move.
Do not roll until the load and papers match.

episodes.title: Chain Gone Slack
episodes.text: You pull over and see one chain hanging slack on the load. The blocks have slid a few inches. Traffic keeps passing close beside you.

choice.prompt: The chain is loose and the load could shift. What do you do first?

options.label: Reset blocks and retighten now
options.outcome: You set your brake, reset the blocks, and crank the binders tight before moving.

options.label: Keep driving to the next stop
options.outcome: You keep rolling and the load shifts more with every turn.

options.label: Just pull the cover tighter
options.outcome: You tug the cover but the chain stays loose underneath it.

episodes.title: Checking Load Papers
episodes.text: You sit in the cab with the load papers on your knee. You check each line for completeness and accuracy. You sign off that the load matches what you carry.

episodes.title: Morning Harness Climb
episodes.text: You arrive at the base of the tower. You pull on your full-body harness and check the straps. You climb slowly toward the components waiting above.

episodes.title: Setting Antenna Mounts
episodes.text: You sit on the tower steel and work on the antenna mounts. You fit a surge arrestor and start the connectors for the transmission line. The mount holes do not line up clean on the first try.

choice.prompt: The mount holes are off by a little. What do you do now?

options.label: Reset and refit the mount
options.outcome: You loosen it and set the mount straight again. It takes more time but the antenna sits level.

options.label: Force the bolts in
options.outcome: You get the bolts started but the mount stays crooked. You will have to redo it before inspection.

episodes.title: Running Cable Again
episodes.text: You run power, ground, and coaxial cables down the tower. You secure them the same way as yesterday. It is the same work you will do tomorrow.

episodes.title: Sweep Testing Lines
episodes.text: You hook up the sweep testing tool to the transmission components. You run the test and watch the trace on the screen. You check the readings for the antennas and tower-mounted amplifiers.

trial.title: Find the fault
trial.scenario: You test the new transmission line with the sweep tool. The trace is steady except for a sharp jump at one connector. The antenna mount and weather proofing look fine.
options: The loose connector on the transmission line
The solid antenna mount
The intact weather proofing
trial.explain: A jump at one point in a sweep trace points to that connector.

episodes.title: Loose Hanger Found
episodes.text: You inspect your completed work across the mounts. You find a hanger not properly fastened and weather proofing lifting at one connector. The antenna also looks a little off level.

choice.prompt: You are still clipped in and light is fading. What do you fix first?

options.label: Refasten the loose hanger and support
options.outcome: You tighten the hanger and confirm the support holds. The cable stops moving and you move on to the seal.

options.label: Reseal the weather proofing first
options.outcome: You press the weather proofing back down around the connector. The cable still shifts at the loose hanger above.

options.label: Re-level the antenna first
options.outcome: You adjust the mount until the antenna reads level. The loose hanger and open seal are still waiting.

episodes.title: Final Tight Check
episodes.text: You go back over the hardware one last time. You check that all hardware is tight and hangers are fastened. You confirm the antennas are level and the support and weather proofing are in place.
